findings.title: Catch block increments retryCount for any error, not just SMS failures
findings.body: The catch block increments retryCount for every exception thrown inside the try, including unrelated failures such as `prisma.profile.findFirst` (DB connection issue), `getCalEventResponses`, `getBookerBaseUrl`, `customTemplate`, and `smsReminderTemplate`. None of these have anything to do with Twilio being unable to schedule the SMS, yet each counts against the 2-retry budget. A transient infrastructure issue in any of those code paths can therefore cause a valid reminder to be auto-deleted on the next cron run before it ever gets a real second chance to reach Twilio. The retry increment should only fire when `twilio.scheduleSMS` actually returns falsy or throws — the other unrelated exceptions should bubble (or be separately handled) without poisoning the retry count.

findings.title: retryCount increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: Both the else branch (line 184) and the catch block (line 195) do `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` based on the value loaded by the earlier `findMany`. Under concurrent execution (manual cron invocations, overlapping cron schedules, retries, etc.) two invocations can both read the same stale value and both write `current+1`, losing one increment and undercounting retries. This can keep a failing reminder alive longer than intended and defeats the PR's goal of bounded retries. Use Prisma's atomic operator, e.g. `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`, and ideally combine with a WHERE clause that also requires the row to still be unscheduled / still have the expected retryCount to avoid duplicate Twilio calls.

findings.title: No tests cover the new retry-and-delete behavior
findings.body: The PR introduces a behavior change with real user-visible consequences (auto-deletion of workflow reminders after 2 failures), adds a new DB column, and changes the cleanup semantics of the existing `deleteMany`. No tests are added to cover: (1) `retryCount` incrementing on `twilio.scheduleSMS` returning falsy, (2) `retryCount` incrementing when the call throws, (3) the new OR-branch of `deleteMany` actually deleting rows with `retryCount > 1`, (4) the boundary case of `retryCount == 1` being retried once more before deletion, and (5) successful sends still setting `scheduled: true`/`referenceId` regardless of retryCount. Without these tests, regressions in retry accounting or the cleanup query can ship unnoticed.

findings.title: Cleanup deleteMany uses retryCount > 1 without a method filter
findings.body: The new branch of the cleanup `deleteMany` matches `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method` constraint, while only the SMS code path ever increments `retryCount`. This silently couples the SMS implementation to the WorkflowReminder table as a whole: any future code that starts incrementing `retryCount` for email or WhatsApp reminders will have those rows deleted by this cron. Either constrain the OR-branch with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, or document and enforce that retryCount is SMS-only.
